section.sectionSummaryBrief: Yosef adds that his descent to Egypt was also desirable for himself, not just for his brothers, and this principle applies to all interpersonal matters.
section.t: However, one could still say,
that even though “for preservation He sent me before you,” nevertheless regarding Yosef himself this was an undesirable matter,
therefore he added:
“It was not you who sent me here, but G-d, and He has made me a father to Pharaoh, etc., and ruler over all the land of Egypt,”
that Yosef’s descent to Egypt was a desirable thing also regarding Yosef.
[And it is noteworthy,
that this is the case in all matters between a person and his fellow.
And as explained in Tanya,
that even when a person does to his fellow the opposite of good,
the truth is that it was from G-d for him,
and one must add,
that from this it is understood that he will have good from it,
for “whatever the Merciful One does, He does for good.”
Except that in the sale of Yosef this was revealed.]

section.sectionSummaryBrief: Our request that G-d be like a brother to us, as Yosef was to his brothers, parallels the soul’s descent into exile and the need to refine the body and animal soul.
section.t: Now, based on the known principle that all matters in the Torah are with utmost precision,
it can be said,
that this that we ask “Who will give you as a brother to me,” in the manner that Yosef acted toward his brothers
[for even though they did an undesirable thing, nevertheless he repaid them with great good],
is,
that every undesirable thing that a person does is analogous to the matter that the tribes did to Yosef when they sold him to Egypt,
and the request “Who will give you as a brother to me” is,
that even though through our deeds, which are not good, we have caused the Holy One, blessed be He, a matter analogous to the sale of Yosef to Egypt
(as will be explained below),
nevertheless He will repay us with good, in the manner that Yosef acted toward his brothers.
And the explanation is,
that the descent of the soul below and its enclothing in the body and the animal soul is actual exile,
and moreover,
that the soul is in captivity and imprisonment
of the body and the animal soul.

And the intention of the soul’s descent below is in order to refine and purify the body and the animal soul and its portion in the world, and to make them vessels for G-dliness, and also so that through the soul’s service below it will ascend to a higher level than it was before its descent.
From this it is understood,
that every moment
that a person does not perform his service,
the pain and suffering of the soul from this, that it is in exile and imprisonment of the body and the animal soul,
are without limit.
For when a person serves G-d,
since through this the intention of the soul’s descent below is fulfilled regarding the two matters mentioned above
[refinement and purification of the body and the animal soul and its portion in the world, and the elevation of the soul],

then the delight of the soul from this, that it fulfills the will of the Holy One, blessed be He, to refine and purify the body, through which the intention of a dwelling place in the lower realms is fulfilled, as well as from its elevation through its service below, is a very great delight,
for which all its suffering from the descent is worthwhile.
But in those moments when a person does not perform his service
[and all the more so in the moments when he does undesirable things],
this that the soul is in exile and imprisonment in the body and the animal soul,
and the pain and suffering it has from this,
are without limit.
And since the soul is literally a part of G-d above,
then the exile and suffering of the soul is
(also)
exile and suffering of the Shechinah.
And this is that through a person’s undesirable conduct
(including also when he does not fulfill his mission,
even when he does not transgress a sin)
he does, as it were, to the Holy One, blessed be He, analogous to what the tribes did to Yosef,
that they sold him as a slave and this later caused him to also be in imprisonment.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: Not heeding the soul’s and Shechinah’s pleas to be released from exile is a greater sin than the undesirable conduct itself, like the brothers’ failure to pity Yosef.
section.t: And another matter in this,
that regarding the act of the tribes toward Yosef it is stated,
“We are guilty… when he pleaded with us and we did not listen…,”
that this not having mercy on him when he pleaded with them is a greater sin than the sale itself,
similarly in the analogy,
that the soul
[and the Shechinah]
plead with the person that he take them out of exile and imprisonment,
and when a person does not listen to the voice of their plea, he is
(in this matter)
worse than the undesirable conduct itself.
